newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's PLA troops cross into HK for handover.
newsitem.headline: China's PLA troops cross into HK for handover.

text.p: About 500 armed troops from Communist China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) streamed across the border into Hong Kong on Monday, just hours ahead of the British colony's handover to Beijing.
The troops, many armed with assault rifles, crossed the border seated in buses or standing erect in open trucks.
Britain and China agreed the troops could cross three hours before Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight (1600 GMT).
Another 4,000 PLA troops will cross the border by land, sea and air six hours after a midnight handover ceremony.
The troops received a rousing send-off in Huang Gang on the Chinese side of the border with twirling lion dancers as well as children banging drums and waving red ribbons.
The Hong Kong side of the border, in a restricted area, had a large banner saying "Warmly Welcome People's Liberation Army" but no crowds and no celebrations.

Elsewhere in the rural Hong Kong side of the border there was a festive mood. Fireworks could be seen and villagers had set up for celebrations. People lined the roads in some places hoping to catch a glimpse of the PLA.
Banners and posters lined the roads cheering Hong Kong's pending reunification with the mainland.
Flowers, signs and colourful ribbons also dotted the roads which the PLA passed along to reach their barracks.
Villages had put up red flags, colourful bunting and signs saying "Peace to the country", "Welcome to the Reunification of Hong Kong with the Mainland".
"People have been celebrating for two days. Everybody is throwing free dinners in the villages," a villager near the Sek Kong military base said.

Many of the 4,700 PLA troops which will be stationed in Hong Kong after the handover are expected to be at Sek Kong, a major military and airforce base used by the British garrison during colonial rule.
Some residents of the thriving capitalist colony have expressed concern over stationing so many PLA troops in Hong Kong, along with their armoured cars, helicopters and ships.
Pro-democracy campaigners in Hong Kong have recalled the crushing of student demonstrations in Beijing in June 1989 by the PLA.
Not all the villagers on the Hong Kong side of the border were happy to see the PLA soldiers arrive.

"There's nothing to celebrate. I've never felt good about China because of the Communists. I guess people my age will always distrust them," said taxi driver Chan Nam, who came to Hong Kong from China in 1960.
Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, will formally cede Hong Kong to China's President Jiang Zemin at midnight, ending 156 years of colonial administration.
